headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, broad-egress code-execution defaults can drive unsafe handoff and leakage risks when paired with Rasa’s chat channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write working directories and use stdin/stdout plus model-provider APIs; Rasa exposes chat channels like Slack, Telegram, and Twilio. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled messages can reach AutoGen through the pair, though the exact default handoff is not documented. Rasa is the ingress side; AutoGen is the parser/executor side.
conditions: IF Rasa forwards user messages into AutoGen prompts or files without sanitization
IF AutoGen treats channel content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict system-prompt delimiter for all Rasa-originated text
Strip tool directives from inbound chat payloads
Require human review before any AutoGen tool call
Use a separate workspace per conversation
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and has broad network egress plus filesystem access; Rasa handles text/voice and can connect to external messaging APIs. If they share a workspace or pass transcripts/files between them, sensitive application data can leak across the pair. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents share the same working directory or transcript store
IF Rasa forwards conversation text into AutoGen context or files
mitigations: Separate storage for transcripts and code artifacts
Redact secrets before any handoff
Disable automatic file attachment in the bridge
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Rasa supports multiple instances only as false, implying a single-instance mutable service. Even without explicit git overlap, both can contend for shared files, logs, or conversation state if orchestrated together. Because shared locking is not documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or state directory
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign distinct directories per agent
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
Use file locks on mutable state
Keep Rasa state in a separate service
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool calls and code execution, while Rasa is a customer-support bot that turns dialogue into responses on external channels. If Rasa consumes AutoGen output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious AutoGen result can cascade into user-facing actions or incorrect support responses. The pairwise pathway is plausible and the blast radius is multi-work-product.
conditions: IF Rasa uses AutoGen-generated text without verification
IF AutoGen output is routed directly into customer-facing replies or actions
mitigations: Require confidence thresholds before publishing replies
Insert a verification step for all AutoGen outputs
Log and review high-impact responses
Limit AutoGen to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add policy-based action gating

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, while Rasa handles text and voice over messaging channels. If regulated customer data flows from Rasa into AutoGen’s external model providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a direct violation.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is sent from Rasa into AutoGen model-provider APIs
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before any handoff
Block regulated fields from model prompts
Align retention settings across both systems
Document a deletion workflow
requires-engineering: add residency and DPA controls
